alt: Section A uses a non-fiction text from Part 1 of the Anthology, printed in the exam, and one previously unseen extract. It is worth 45 marks in about 1 hour 30 minutes including reading time. Students should read journalism, speeches, journals, reference books and literary non-fiction; transient texts such as instant news feeds and advertisements are not assessed.
caption: One known Anthology text, one unseen extract, 45 marks.

alt: Explicit information is told: “The village had no road” gives a fact. Implicit information is worked out: she “rationed the last of the batteries” suggests the journey had gone on longer than planned and she felt anxious. Three habits: stay inside the line range, make one point per piece of evidence, and use your own words when told to.
caption: Select precisely, infer from evidence, one point at a time.

after: ## Skill 2: AO2, analysing language and structure
alt: A table of eight non-fiction devices and their typical effects, from anecdote and direct address to structural shifts and an ending that circles back to the opening image. Structural devices are highlighted because they are the ones most often left out.
caption: Cover structure as well as language in every AO2 answer.

after: ## Worked example on an original unseen extract
alt: A four-step chain on the original rescue passage: method (a short, flat opening sentence), evidence (“The call came at 2 a.m., as they always do”), effect (the emergency feels routine) and reason (the reader senses her long experience). The passage also omits the search and ends with “eleven times” and “I counted” to turn anger into amused sympathy.
caption: Name the method, quote briefly, explain the effect and why the writer wants it.

after: ## Skill 3: AO3, comparing ideas and perspectives
alt: AO3 has two halves: links between ideas and perspectives, and how these are conveyed. Perspectives include insider or outsider, participant or observer, approving or critical, certain or uncertain. Morris’s article reports detachedly and invites judgement with its headline; the rescuer writes from inside the event with first-person honesty and ends with sympathy.
caption: Compare what the writers think and how they convey it, in every paragraph.

alt: A bar of Section A’s 45 marks in proportion: AO1 11, AO2 12 and AO3 22, with the largest block of time protected for the comparison. Below, a three-row planning grid: shared idea, Text 1 perspective and method, Text 2 perspective and method.
caption: Give the 22-mark comparison the most time, and plan it in a grid.
